interest: This document is particularly valuable to historians of U.S.-Japan diplomatic and economic relations during the interwar period as it illuminates the persistent jurisdictional and commercial tensions surrounding Japanese taxation of American citizens and corporations. The list tracks the practical application and contested interpretations of the Treaty of 1911, specifically regarding whether assessment methods on American insurance companies and corporations constituted unlawful discrimination in favor of domestic Japanese entities. Furthermore, the docket entries and cross-references document contentious transitional issues following the abolition of extraterritoriality, including the taxation of income derived from perpetual leaseholds in former treaty ports like Yokohama and the resistance by foreign missions (American, British, German, and French) to Japanese tax authorities seeking information on local consulate employees in Kobe on the eve of the Second Sino-Japanese War.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department Record Group 59, decimal file 894.5123, File 273) consists of a two-page "List of Papers" (docket sheets) indexing official communications and cross-references regarding Japanese income taxation affecting American interests between 1923 and 1937. The indexed documents address assessments on American insurance companies (such as the Home Insurance Company of New York and Continental Insurance Company of New York), income taxes levied on Americans doing business in Japan under the Treaty of 1911, and the tax status of American clerks and Japanese employees at the Nagasaki Consulate. The docket also records internal State Department correspondence concerning alleged discrimination favoring Japanese corporations over American corporations, as well as cross-references to related decimal files concerning income taxes on American government officials, taxes on income from perpetual lease properties in Yokohama, general Japanese income tax legislation, and requests by Japanese revenue authorities in Kobe for employee records.

subfiles.about: A two-page Department of State list of papers docket indexing correspondence and cross-reference sheets concerning Japanese income taxation affecting Americans between 1923 and 1937.
subfiles.summary: This two-page List of Papers serves as the central docket register for Department of State decimal file 894.5123, indexing communications concerning Japanese income taxation from 1923 to 1937. Page 1 records despatches and a telegram concerning excess income taxes assessed on American insurance companies, taxes levied on American businessmen under the Treaty of 1911, and the tax liabilities of Nagasaki consular staff. Page 2 (recorded as Page 7 of the docket registry) notes correspondence on alleged corporate tax discrimination favoring domestic Japanese firms and cross-references files regarding taxation of American officials, perpetual lease property in Yokohama, general Japanese tax laws, and consular employee information furnished to local revenue authorities in Kobe.
